blurb: Tiny spaniel in two ear types: the erect-eared Papillon and the drop-eared Phalène
description: The Continental Toy Spaniel is a Belgian and French toy spaniel, about 28 cm tall, with a mostly white coat and erect (Papillon) or drooping (Phalène) ears.
answer: The Continental Toy Spaniel, or Épagneul Nain Continental, is a toy-sized spaniel from Belgium and France. It comes in two forms that differ only in the ears: the erect-eared Papillon and the drop-eared Phalène. It stands about 28 cm and weighs roughly 1.5 to 5 kg.

body: Lapdogs of miniature spaniel type appear in European paintings from the sixteenth century onwards, including works by Titian, Veronese and Watteau. The American Kennel Club first recognized the Papillon in 1935. A Papillon won Best in Show at Westminster in 1999, and another at Crufts in 2019, each a first for the breed.

The coat is predominantly white with patches of any colour; only on the head does the colour exceed the white. Height is up to about 28 cm, with two weight classes, 1.5 to 2.5 kg and 2.5 to 5 kg. The Papillon (French for butterfly) has upright ears, while the Phalène (French for moth) has dropped, spaniel-like ears. The AKC and the FCI treat both as one breed.
The source text gives little detail on temperament. Papillons are noted for success in obedience and agility as well as the show ring.
Sources give little specific detail on care. Like most small, active companion breeds, it is generally thought to benefit from daily walks, play and routine brushing.

A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 14.5 years for the breed, compared to an average of 12.7 for purebreeds. Health concerns are described as minor, but conditions reported in the breed include patellar luxation, seizures, dental problems, progressive retinal atrophy, intervertebral disk disease and allergies.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Papillon and a Phalène?
faq.a: Only the ears: the Papillon has erect ears and the Phalène has drooping ones. In all other respects they are identical and are treated as one breed by the AKC and the FCI.

faq.q: How big does a Continental Toy Spaniel get?
faq.a: It stands up to about 28 cm at the withers and weighs between 1.5 and 5 kg, split into two weight classes.
A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 14.5 years for the breed.

faq.q: Is the Continental Toy Spaniel recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It is FCI breed number 77 in Group 9, Companion and Toy Dogs.
